newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Soft in thin talks amid weak swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Soft in thin talks amid weak swaps.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil was weaker on Wednesday but some players were still looking for support from China, traders said.
"We are all expecting China to come back to the market and buy for March and some people said they are already back," said one trader.
"But it seems many of the Chinese players are still away from the market," he added.
Supplies remained sufficient and some Middle East sellers are still looking for buyers, traders said.
One independent said fuel oil was under pressure to rise because China was heard making enquiries, but another said he did not expect much Chinese activity in the near term.
"I think China at least has covered the first half of March," said the second trader.
Between five and seven 80,000-tonne cargoes are shipped to this region on a monthly basis from the Middle East with arbitrage cargoes also seen from Venezuela, traders said.
March fuel oil swaps quotes were slightly firmer to $103.00/$104.00 per tonne from $102.75/$103.50 on Tuesday.
In the LSWR market, talks were thin and buying interest was seen at $21 per barrel.
Indonesia's state oil company, Pertamina, allocated a total of 3.7 million barrels of LSWR for loading in March, the same amount allocated in February, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
